ActiveGame.description: The game a user is currently in (the dispatcher's redirect target).
ActiveGame.title: ActiveGame

ArmySize.description:
The army size rule: ``base + per_barracks × barracks level + held sites ÷
sites_per_point``, never above ``ceiling``. Your own base is not a held site.
ArmySize.title: ArmySize

Axial.description:
An axial hex coordinate.

``q`` is the column-ish axis and ``r`` the row-ish axis. Frozen so two
coordinates with the same values are equal and hashable.
Axial.title: Axial

BarrageHit.description:
The unit struck by a barrage and its outcome (SPEC §7.2, §13.1).

A barrage targets a hex; this records the unit that happened to occupy it.
The occupant is a stationary defender, so terrain/Hold modifiers apply
(SPEC §12.10); artillery fires at range, so there is no retaliation.
BarrageHit.title: BarrageHit

BarrageOrder.description: Artillery fires at a visible target hex within range (SPEC §7.2).
BarrageOrder.title: BarrageOrder

BarrageResolved.description:
An artillery Barrage order resolved against ``target`` (SPEC §7.2, §11.3).

``hit`` is the struck unit, or ``None`` when the target hex was empty (a
single, well-defined meaning: barrage targets a hex, which may hold nobody).
BarrageResolved.title: BarrageResolved

Building.description: A building at a player's base, upgraded level by level.
Building.title: Building

BuildingLevel.description: What one level of a building costs and how many turns it takes to build.
BuildingLevel.title: BuildingLevel

ClockRunView.description: Returned by the clock endpoint: worlds resolved, and those already done.
ClockRunView.title: ClockRunView

ColumnHeld.description:
A column waited this pulse because ``target`` already holds a full stack.

Unlike `MoveBlocked`, the column keeps its order and tries again next pulse.
ColumnHeld.title: ColumnHeld

ColumnStuck.description: A column had to deploy but no hex within reach was free; it stays packed.
ColumnStuck.title: ColumnStuck

CombatParticipant.description:
One unit's contribution to and outcome in a combat event (SPEC §16.3).

Damage is reported as totals: ``damage_dealt`` is summed across every
opposing unit this one struck, ``damage_taken`` across every opponent that
struck it. For a 1v1 these are the single exchanged values in the §16.3
example; in a dogpile each attacker's ``damage_dealt`` is its hit on the
defender, and the defender's ``damage_dealt`` is the sum of its full
retaliation against every attacker (SPEC §12.4).
CombatParticipant.title: CombatParticipant

CombatResolved.description:
A single combat over one contested ``coord`` in ``pulse`` (SPEC §12).

Holds everything needed to render the §16.3 explanation: every participant
with its role, modifiers, damage, and fate, plus the occupation outcome.
``entrant_id`` is the surviving lead entrant that occupied the hex, or
``None`` if nobody entered (opposing survivors remained, or all entrants
died — SPEC §12.5). ``entrant_continued`` records whether that entrant had
movement pulses left and kept moving (SPEC §11.2/§12.5).
CombatResolved.title: CombatResolved

CombatRole.description:
A unit's role in a combat event (SPEC §12).

``DEFENDER`` is the stationary occupant of the contested hex — the only
participant that receives terrain/Hold modifiers (SPEC §12.10). ``ATTACKER``
covers every unit moving into the hex (an into-enemy attack, an empty-hex
contest, or an edge swap); attackers never get terrain/Hold bonuses.
CombatRole.title: CombatRole

CommandCap.description:
A unit cap that grows with holdings (WORLD_SPEC §7).

A player may field ``base + per_town × towns + per_city × cities`` units, up
to ``ceiling``: land, not grinding, grows an army.
CommandCap.title: CommandCap

CompactMap.description:
A map as two row-major offset grids flattened to strings.

``terrain[row * width + col]`` is the terrain character of grid cell
``(col, row)``; ``roads`` is the same shape with `ROAD_CHAR` for a road and
`NO_ROAD_CHAR` for none.
CompactMap.title: CompactMap

Construction.description:
A building level under construction at a player's base.

Paid for when it starts; it completes in the economy phase of turn
``completes_on``.
Construction.title: Construction

ConstructionCompleted.description: A building reached a new level.
ConstructionCompleted.title: ConstructionCompleted

ConstructionStarted.description: A player paid for and began a building level at their base.
ConstructionStarted.title: ConstructionStarted

ConstructionVoided.description: A build order was skipped; nothing was paid.
ConstructionVoided.title: ConstructionVoided

ConstructionVoidedReason.description: Why a submission-legal build order did not start this turn.
ConstructionVoidedReason.title: ConstructionVoidedReason

CreateGameRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /games``: which authored scenario to instantiate.

``vs_bot`` requests a game against the computer (AI_SPEC §9): the service
fills the second slot with a bot player and the game starts immediately.
``bot_policy`` picks the AI (resolved via `app.ai.arena`'s registry) and is
only consulted when ``vs_bot`` is true.
CreateGameRequest.title: CreateGameRequest

CreateWorldRequest.description: Body for ``POST /dev/worlds``: the world to generate and how many bots.
CreateWorldRequest.title: CreateWorldRequest

DeployOrder.description: A column unpacks where it stands, ready to fight next turn (WORLD_SPEC §4.5).
DeployOrder.title: DeployOrder

DevProfile.description:
A selectable account in the dev profile switcher.

The switcher lists the calling dev's own account plus the ``@hex.local`` test
accounts, so a dev picks who to impersonate from a menu rather than pasting a
raw user id. ``is_self`` marks the dev's real account.
DevProfile.title: DevProfile

DispatchView.description:
Where login should send a user: their active game, or nothing (start screen).

``active_game`` is ``None`` with exactly one meaning — the user holds no slot in
any un-finished game, so the frontend shows the create / paste-join screen.
DispatchView.title: DispatchView

EconomyResolved.description:
One player's muster accounting for the turn (SPEC §6.2–6.4, §11.3 Phase 5).

``net`` is ``income - upkeep`` (may be negative; the shortfall is paid from the
bank, which floors at 0). ``lost_to_cap`` is muster discarded because the bank
would exceed its cap (SPEC §6.4). ``bank_after`` is the resulting bank.
EconomyResolved.title: EconomyResolved

Facing.description:
Which way a unit's sprite faces on the board: left or right only.

Purely cosmetic render state — the game has no facing *mechanic* (movement is
pulses, combat is omnidirectional). It exists so the client can mirror one
sprite horizontally instead of authoring per-direction art (roadmap Phase 8,
slice U0). Semantics: a unit faces the way it last moved — its final completed
move step of the turn reduced to a net horizontal sign on the flat-top board's
``q`` axis (rightward → `RIGHT`, leftward → `LEFT`; a purely vertical step
keeps the prior facing). No rotation, no 8-way. `RIGHT` is the default.
Facing.title: Facing

GameConfig.description:
Per-game limits and victory config (SPEC §6.1, §6.4, §15).

``command_cap``, when set, replaces the flat ``unit_cap`` with a cap that grows
with holdings (still never above ``unit_cap``). ``settlement_repair`` is the
HP a unit resting in a town or city regains per turn. World games set both
(WORLD_SPEC §7); v0.1 games keep the defaults.
GameConfig.title: GameConfig

GameHistoryEntry.description:
One row of a user's game history (account screen).

``outcome`` is from the caller's perspective: ``win``/``loss``/``draw`` once the
game is decided, else ``in_progress`` (a lobby or active game). ``turn`` is the
current/final turn number; ``created_at`` is the game's ISO creation timestamp.
GameHistoryEntry.title: GameHistoryEntry

GameMap.description:
Static board geometry: dimensions and the terrain of every hex.

Holds only content that does not change during play. Dynamic facts
(settlement control, unit positions) live on `GameState`, not here.

Frozen, so engine phases share one map between successive states instead of
deep-copying it (a world map is ~10^5 hexes; WORLD_SPEC §10). `index` is a
lazily built coord → hex lookup, safe to cache because the map never changes.
GameMap.title: GameMap

GameState.description:
The canonical, serializable state of one game at one turn.

This is the blob stored in the ``games`` row and the value threaded through
the engine: ``resolve_turn(state, orders) -> (new_state, event_log)``.
Lookups (`hex_at`, `unit_at`, `settlement_at`) are convenience helpers built
on demand; the stored representation is plain lists so it serializes cleanly
(axial coords can't be JSON object keys).
GameState.title: GameState

GameView.description:
A player's fog-filtered view of a game (SPEC §9).

``state`` is redacted to the caller's perspective: enemy units on hexes the
caller cannot see are removed (the map, settlement control, and banks are
public in v0.1). ``victory`` is the authoritative global outcome. ``visible``
is the set of hexes the caller's units currently illuminate (SPEC §9), so the
frontend can dim everything outside it as fog of war; the map itself is public,
so fog is a rendering hint, not a redaction.
GameView.title: GameView

Hex.description:
A single map cell: its coordinate, base terrain, and road layer.

``road`` is a layer on top of terrain (SPEC §3.3, §4.1): a unit whose entire
path follows connected road hexes gets +1 movement. A bridge hex (terrain
``BRIDGE``) is what a road becomes where it crosses a river (SPEC §3.4).
Frozen: the map is static for the life of a game.
Hex.title: Hex

HoldOrder.description: Do not move; gain a defensive bonus if attacked (SPEC §7.4).
HoldOrder.title: HoldOrder

JoinGameRequest.description: Body for ``POST /games/{id}/join``: the invite token from the share link.
JoinGameRequest.title: JoinGameRequest

MapSite.description:
A site's static role in a world economy, fixed at generation.

A site is the ownership-bearing thing in a world (VISION §6): its `Settlement`
record in the state says who holds it. A city site stands on its city hex; a
farm, oil field, steel mill, factory or base stands on its own plains hex
beside a town or a road (towns themselves hold no ownership in a world).
``garrison`` is the tier (1–4) of the neutral garrison the site starts with,
or 0 for a base, which is never garrisoned. It stays on the map after the
garrison is gone so the strategic view can always show how hard a site was.
``level`` (1–3) raises a farm's, oil field's, steel mill's or factory's
income; cities and bases are always level 1. It defaults so maps stored
before levels existed still decode.
MapSite.title: MapSite

MarchOrder.description:
Travel as a column along an exact path (WORLD_SPEC §4.4, §5).

A deployed unit packs first (the opening pulses of the turn) and then
marches; a column marches from pulse 1. Steps cost pulses (road vs off-road)
rather than one per pulse. With ``deploy_on_arrival`` the unit deploys, clean,
at the end of the turn in which it completes the path.
MarchOrder.title: MarchOrder

MeView.description:
The authenticated caller's own identity and dev role.

Backs the frontend dev profile switcher: ``is_dev`` decides whether the switcher
is shown, and reflects the *real* account (impersonation is not applied).
MeView.title: MeView

MoveBlocked.description: A unit's attempted step into ``target`` failed; it stops for the turn.
MoveBlocked.title: MoveBlocked

MoveBlockedReason.description: Why a unit's attempted step failed and ended its movement (SPEC §11.3).
MoveBlockedReason.title: MoveBlockedReason

MoveOrder.description:
Follow an exact planned path of adjacent hexes (SPEC §7.1).

``path`` is the sequence of hexes to enter, in order, one per movement
pulse. Combat occurs if enemy contact happens; the unit does not reroute if
blocked.
MoveOrder.title: MoveOrder

OrderMooted.description:
A unit's order was dropped because the turn voided it before it applied.

Barrage (§11.3 Phase 1) removes destroyed units before movement (Phase 2), so a
statically-legal Move/Hold/Rest order can name a unit that no longer exists by
the time movement resolves. That is defined simultaneity, not a caller bug: the
order is skipped and this event records it for the replay. Emitted between the
barrage events and the movement events. (An order naming a unit that *never*
existed remains a caller bug and still raises `EngineError` in movement. A
Barrage order whose artillery died in the exchange is *not* mooted — barrage
resolves simultaneously, so that order already applied in Phase 1.)

``owner`` is carried on the event because the unit is destroyed: fog filtering
runs against the post-turn state, where the dead unit can no longer be resolved
to its owner.
OrderMooted.title: OrderMooted

OrderMootedReason.description: Why a statically-legal order became moot mid-turn (SPEC §11.3).
OrderMootedReason.title: OrderMootedReason

Player.description:
A participant's mutable economy state (SPEC §6, economy draft).

``bank`` is the v0.1 muster bank, clamped to 0..`GameConfig.muster_bank_cap`
by the economy phase (SPEC §6.3, §6.4). A world game uses ``stocks``,
``buildings`` and ``construction`` instead and leaves ``bank`` at 0.
``buildings`` maps a building to its completed level; a building never built
is absent (level 0). ``construction`` is ``None`` when nothing is being built.
Settlement control is not duplicated here — derive it from
`GameState.settlements` to keep one source of truth.
Player.title: Player

PlayerCredentials.description:
Returned on create/join: which slot the caller now holds, and the share link.

Identity is the Supabase JWT (not returned here); ``invite_token`` lets the
holder share the open slot.
PlayerCredentials.title: PlayerCredentials

Posture.description:
How a unit is set up (WORLD_SPEC §4).

``DEPLOYED`` is the v0.1 unit: one per hex, exerts and obeys ZOC, fights.
``COLUMN`` is packed for travel: fast, stacks with friendly columns, exerts no
ZOC, cannot attack, and defends badly.
Posture.title: Posture

Recruitment.description:
A planning-phase request to recruit a new unit (SPEC §6.5).

Recruitment is not a per-unit `Order` — it creates a unit that does not exist
yet, so it has no ``unit_id``. A request names the owning player, the unit
``type`` to build, and the friendly-city ``coord`` to deploy it on; the
recruitment phase validates affordability, the unit cap, and placement, then
assigns the new unit's id (SPEC §11.3 Phase 6).
Recruitment.title: Recruitment

RecruitmentVoided.description:
A recruit request was skipped because the turn voided it (SPEC §6.5, §11.3).

Recruitment resolves last (§11.3 Phase 6), after movement/capture/economy, so a
statically-legal recruit can be voided by the turn itself: the city was captured
(possibly by a fog-hidden enemy), a unit ended its move on the hex, the running
unit cap filled, or the post-economy bank fell short. The muster stays banked and
the request is skipped rather than crashing the turn.
RecruitmentVoided.title: RecruitmentVoided

RecruitmentVoidedReason.description: Why a submission-legal recruit was voided by the turn (SPEC §6.5, §11.3).
RecruitmentVoidedReason.title: RecruitmentVoidedReason

RestOrder.description: Do not move; repair HP if undamaged during execution (SPEC §7.3).
RestOrder.title: RestOrder

Settlement.description:
Dynamic ownership of a settlement hex (SPEC §3.2, §14).

The settlement's *kind* is static map data, not stored here, so there is one
source of truth: in a v0.1 game it is the terrain at ``coord``
(``Terrain.TOWN``/``Terrain.CITY``); in a world it is the `MapSite` at
``coord`` (every site but a vacant base slot has a settlement, and towns have
none). This record carries only the part that changes during play:
``controlled_by``, where ``None`` means neutral / uncontrolled (a single,
well-defined meaning). Control changes only via the capture phase (SPEC §14.1).
Settlement.title: Settlement

SettlementCaptured.description:
An infantry/armor unit captured a settlement (SPEC §14.1, §11.3 Phase 3).

Emitted only when control actually changes — a unit sitting on a settlement
it already controls produces no event. ``previous_owner`` is ``None`` when the
settlement was neutral before capture (a single, well-defined meaning).
``settlement`` is the terrain of the captured hex: in a v0.1 game that is what
was taken (town or city). ``site`` is the world site that was taken (farm,
base, …), whose hex is usually plains; it is ``None`` exactly when the hex is
not a world site, which is every v0.1 capture (and events stored before the
field existed).
SettlementCaptured.title: SettlementCaptured

SiteKind.description:
What a site is in a world economy, fixed when the map is generated.

The kind decides what a site produces and what may be recruited there. A
`CITY` stands on its city hex; every other kind stands on its own plains hex
beside a town or a road. A `BASE` is a player's home: not a city, one per slot,
on open ground with a four-hex plot kept clear around it.
SiteKind.title: SiteKind

StandingTravel.description:
A travel order still in progress, carried from turn to turn (WORLD_SPEC §5).

``route`` is the hexes the unit has yet to enter, in order, fixed when the
order was issued (routes are planned over the static map, so they never need
recomputing). Each turn the unit has no fresh order, the engine marches it
along ``route``; the order ends on arrival, contact, an explicit order, or the
unit's destruction. ``on_arrival`` is the posture to finish in.
StandingTravel.title: StandingTravel

Stocks.description: An amount of each resource: a stockpile, an income, a cost or an upkeep.
Stocks.title: Stocks

StocksResolved.description:
One world player's resource accounting for the turn (economy draft §02).

``after = before + income - upkeep``, floored at 0 and limited to storage;
``lost_to_storage`` is what the depot could not hold. A shortfall below 0
disbands a unit (`UnitDisbanded`).
StocksResolved.title: StocksResolved

SubmitOrdersRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /games/{id}/orders``: a player's full plan for the turn.

Both lists default to empty: a player may legitimately submit no orders (every
unit holds) and no recruits. FastAPI parses ``orders`` into the discriminated
`Order` union, so unknown order shapes are rejected as 422 at the wire.
SubmitOrdersRequest.title: SubmitOrdersRequest

SubmitResult.description: Outcome of submitting orders: always locked; executed iff all players in.
SubmitResult.title: SubmitResult

Terrain.description:
Terrain of a hex (SPEC §4.1).

Town and City are terrain types in their own right — a settlement hex *is*
town/city terrain, not a marker layered on plains/woods. Their dynamic
ownership is tracked separately by `app.engine.models.Settlement`, but the
terrain identity, defense bonus, and income all live here. Road, by
contrast, is a boolean modifier layered onto terrain (`Hex.road`).

In a world game ownership lives on sites instead (`MapSite`, VISION §6): a
town there is terrain only, and a farm, oil field, steel mill, factory or base
stands on its own plains hex. Rules that ask "is this settlement ground?" go
through `GameState.settlement_ground`, which covers both.
Terrain.title: Terrain

TrafficJam.description:
Friendly units collided on ``coord`` in the same pulse (SPEC §8.2).

None of them entered; all of them stop for the turn. ``unit_ids`` is sorted
for deterministic replay.
TrafficJam.title: TrafficJam

TravelEndReason.description: Why a standing travel order ended (WORLD_SPEC §5).
TravelEndReason.title: TravelEndReason

TravelEnded.description:
A unit's standing travel order is finished, for ``reason``.

Private to the owner, like the order itself: other players see the column
move and deploy, never where it was headed. ``coord`` is where the unit
stands (or fell) when the order ended.
TravelEnded.title: TravelEnded

TravelOrder.description:
Go to a destination as a column, over as many turns as it takes (WORLD_SPEC §5).

The engine plans the route (cheapest column path over the static map,
through the optional ``via`` waypoints in order), packs the unit if it is
deployed, and keeps it marching every turn it has no fresh order. It finishes
in the ``on_arrival`` posture. Contact ends the order early: the column
deploys where it meets the enemy.
TravelOrder.title: TravelOrder

TurnReplay.description: A resolved turn's replay: the event log, resulting state, victory snapshot.
TurnReplay.title: TurnReplay

Unit.description:
A single unit instance (SPEC §5).

Static type stats (move, attack, vision, …) are looked up from
`app.engine.stats.UNIT_STATS` by ``type``; only per-instance state lives
here. ``hp`` is clamped to 0..10 (SPEC §5.2); a unit at 0 HP is destroyed.

``facing`` is cosmetic render state (see `Facing`): the left/right direction
the sprite faces, set by the unit's last movement. It defaults so state JSONB
persisted before this field existed still validates (older games load with
the default facing).

``posture`` is deployed or column (WORLD_SPEC §4). ``disordered`` marks a unit
that auto-deployed on contact: it defends worse and cannot attack until the
end of the next turn's execution (WORLD_SPEC §4.5). Both default so older
persisted states load as deployed, ordered units.
Unit.title: Unit

UnitDeployed.description:
A column unpacked at ``dest`` (``origin`` unless it spilled to a free hex).

``disordered`` is set for unplanned deployments (contact, barrage): the unit
defends worse and cannot attack through the end of the next turn.
UnitDeployed.title: UnitDeployed

UnitDisbanded.description:
A shortage disbanded a unit (economy draft §02).

``shortage`` is the resource that ran out. ``chosen`` is whether the unit was
the player's own pick, rather than the weakest qualifying unit by default.
UnitDisbanded.title: UnitDisbanded

UnitMoved.description: A unit successfully stepped from ``origin`` to ``dest`` in ``pulse``.
UnitMoved.title: UnitMoved

UnitPacked.description: A deployed unit finished packing and is a column from ``pulse`` on.
UnitPacked.title: UnitPacked

UnitRecruited.description:
A player recruited a new unit at a friendly city (SPEC §6.5, §11.3 Phase 6).

``unit_id`` is the id assigned to the new unit; ``bank_after`` is the player's
bank once ``cost`` was deducted.
UnitRecruited.title: UnitRecruited

UnitRepaired.description:
A resting, undamaged unit recovered HP (SPEC §7.3, §11.3 Phase 4).

Emitted only when HP actually increases. ``in_settlement`` records whether the
unit rested on settlement ground (a town/city, or a founded world site: the
+2-up-to-10 tier) versus anywhere else (the +1-up-to-7 tier).
UnitRepaired.title: UnitRepaired

VictoryConfig.description:
Scenario-defined victory parameters (SPEC §15).

Defaults match the recommended v0.1 rules: lose at zero controlled cities,
otherwise score settlements at the turn limit (town=1, city=3).
VictoryConfig.title: VictoryConfig

VictoryStatus.description:
The outcome of a victory check (SPEC §15).

``winner`` is set only on a decisive result; it is ``None`` when the game is
ongoing (``reason == ONGOING``) or drawn (a decided ``reason`` with no single
winner). ``eliminated`` lists players controlling zero cities while city
elimination is in effect. ``scores`` is each player's settlement victory-point
total (§15.2), always computed so a UI can show standings mid-game.
VictoryStatus.title: VictoryStatus

WorldEconomy.description:
Every tunable number of the world economy (defaults: draft revision 2).

A site earns ``site_income[kind]`` at level 1 and ``level_income[kind]`` more
per level above 1 (`income`); cities and bases are always level 1.
``buildings[b][k]`` is level ``k + 1`` of building ``b``. ``storage[k]`` is
the per-resource stockpile limit at depot level ``k``, so it has one more
entry than the depot has levels. Artillery needs a workshop and armor a held
factory; those unlock rules are fixed in the recruitment phase.
WorldEconomy.title: WorldEconomy

WorldReplay.description: A resolved world turn for one viewer: witnessed events and the fogged state.
WorldReplay.title: WorldReplay

WorldState.description:
A world `GameState` without its static map.

A world map is ~10^5 hexes, so the client fetches it once
(``GET /worlds/{id}/map``) and every per-turn payload carries this instead.
The fields mirror `GameState` minus ``map``; a test keeps them in step.
WorldState.title: WorldState

WorldSummary.description: A running world as the join screen lists it (``GET /worlds``).
WorldSummary.title: WorldSummary

WorldUnitRecruited.description: A world player recruited a unit, paying ``cost`` from their stocks.
WorldUnitRecruited.title: WorldUnitRecruited

WorldView.description:
A player's fog-filtered view of a world (the map comes separately).

``submission`` is the caller's plan for this turn as last submitted, which they
may revise until the turn resolves; ``None`` means they have submitted nothing
this turn. The turn itself resolves on the world's clock, not when everyone
is in.
WorldView.title: WorldView

get.description:
List the accounts the dev switcher can impersonate.

Dev-only (403 otherwise). Returns the calling dev's own account plus every
``@hex.local`` test account, read server-side via the service-role admin API.

schema.title: Response Dev Profiles Dev Profiles Get

With ``vs_bot`` the remaining slot is filled by an AI opponent and the game
starts immediately (AI_SPEC §9).

The caller's game history (newest first) for the account screen.

Validate and lock the caller's orders; resolve the turn if both are in.
Concede the caller's slot; ends the game if they were the last rival.

Liveness probe for Cloud Run and uptime checks. No external dependencies.

Demonstrates the full browser -> Cloud Run -> Supabase chain: the counts are
